title: Finite fibre-generic valuation sets and the modification locus
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed, def-weil-field], let $V\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $K$ whose prime ideals form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be a normal flat finitely presented $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one with smooth generic fibre and finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Normal means that its local rings are integrally closed domains. Write $\mathcal V(C)$ for the disjoint union over components of the spaces of centred valuations of their function fields, with the centre-projection topology of [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods]. A centred valuation is a valuation subring $O$ of a component function field $L$, with fraction field $L$, together with a $T$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}O\to C$ inducing the generic-point map. For a reduced modification $q:Y\to C$, put $\Gamma(Y)=\{\nu\in\mathcal V(C):\text{ the centre of the proper lift of }\nu\text{ is a generic point of its }T\text{-fibre}\}$ and $\Gamma_0(Y)=\{\nu\in\Gamma(Y):\text{ the centre of }\nu\text{ on }C\text{ is closed in }C\}$. Here a modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] inducing an isomorphism between schematically dense opens of source and target; schematically dense means that restriction of the structure sheaf to the open is injective. Reduced means no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme].

The set $\Gamma_0(Y)$ is finite, every member of $\Gamma(Y)$ satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(O\cap K)}\kappa(O)=1$, and
$$\Gamma(Y)=\operatorname{gen}(\Gamma_0(Y))\cup\Gamma(C).$$
Here $\operatorname{gen}$ takes all generalizations in $\mathcal V(C)$, and $\Gamma(C)$ refers to the identity modification. Each $\Gamma(Y)$ is closed under generalization. Every fibre-generic point of $Y$ is the centre of some member of $\Gamma(Y)$; when $Y$ is normal this correspondence is bijective. Finally, the modification locus of $q$, the closed complement of its largest isomorphism open in $C$, is quasi-finite over $T$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Residue fields and transcendence degree have the meanings of [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree].

The reduced-source formulation follows by the finite normalization discussed in Section 4.1 (printed p. 25): finite normalization does not change which valuations have fibre-generic centres.
